Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Angola's SEPE portal (sepe.gov.ao), launched in 2019, requires registration using unique Taxpayer and Identity Card (BI) numbers. The SEPE login page explicitly references 'Identidade Digital' (Digital Identity) as an authentication mechanism. Services include scheduling appointments, consulting citizenship documents, social security numbers, and company registration. A face recognition system had not been introduced as of the e-governance report, but ID number-based portal authentication is operational.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The Angolan biometric ID card (Bilhete de Identidade) collects 10 fingerprints, photograph, signature and height at enrollment. The card chip stores a fingerprint image (right forefinger). The system established via public-private partnership with DGM Sistemas and HID Global also captures iris data as reported by the Greater Internet Freedom 2023 country report. Facial image collection is referenced in legislation (2015 Birth Registration Simplification Act) though not yet fully implemented system-wide.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Angola has a partially deployed biometric national ID system (Bilhete de Identidade, BI) using fingerprints and iris data, backed by a centralised PGIBI database and 243 fixed/mobile issuance centres operated via public-private partnership with DGM Sistemas, HID Global and Unisys Africa. As of 2022/2023, 46% of the population holds a BI card. A full digital ID solution (modelled on India's Aadhaar) is in planning/design stage supported by World Bank Angola Digital Acceleration Project and a 2025 India-Angola DPI partnership. The system is partially deployed nationwide but not yet fully operational as a digital ID.
